# SpeechKit

SpeechKit is a local-first voice framework with three explicit voice contracts:
Dictation turns speech into text, Assist handles a one-shot request with optional
TTS, and Voice Agent holds a realtime conversation. Meeting is a separate
recording and notes service alongside those modes.

Use the Windows desktop app for Dictation, Assist, Voice Agent and Meeting.
The macOS 14+ Apple Silicon app is an ad-hoc signed, Dictation-only beta.
Android offers public Kotlin SDK modules and a keyboard/system-assistant
reference app in testing; Voice Agent needs a SpeechKit Server. Browser clients
use TypeScript packages and framework-neutral Voice UI components. Linux is a
self-hosted server target, not a desktop app download.

Embed public Go packages without a SpeechKit Server, or connect clients over
HTTP/WebSocket. Local Dictation needs a whisper.cpp runtime and model but no
cloud key. Choose providers through the running catalog and readiness metadata;
available models and capabilities depend on the configured route. Words and
Replacements customize recognition and final text. Hands-Free is an activation
layer for the voice modes.

Meeting on Windows captures microphone and system audio separately, combines
the transcript with your notes and a template into a Meeting Review, and never
persists meeting audio. Review generation needs a configured local or cloud
model. Channel labels do not identify each remote participant. The public
pkg/speechkit/meeting runtime supports host-owned capture adapters and notes
helpers; examples/meeting/synthetic-host demonstrates it without devices or
credentials. Do not assume the full desktop Meeting workflow has a server REST,
SSE or TypeScript equivalent. Use only endpoints present in the server OpenAPI.

Generate a working starter project:

- `speechkit-cli init --list`: see embedded templates.
- `speechkit-cli init --template browser-dictation-react my-app`: scaffold a Vite + React + TypeScript dictation app.
- Or via MCP: `speechkit_scaffold_integration` returns the same starter files in-band without writing to the host.
- Native Android memo showcase prompt: create a real Gradle Android project with `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, Kotlin/Java sources, configurable `SPEECHKIT_SERVER_URL`/token settings, a fresh Docker Compose SpeechKit Server, Dictation `/v1/dictation/transcribe`, Assist `/v1/assist/process`, and a `verifySpeechKitLive` Gradle task that writes `speechkit-one-shot-functional-result.json` with `status=pass`, `manifest_file=speechkit-one-shot-manifest.json`, and `checked_via_app=true`.

Embed a Voice Agent into your own app:

- Reference: `examples/voice-agent/game-instructor/` (TOML preset + Go embedder + README).
- Provider-switching reference: `examples/voice-agent/provider-switching/`
  (credential-free fake provider, real public descriptors).
- One prompt: "Build a 15-minute voice-agent game instructor into my app using SpeechKit. Use `pkg/speechkit/client` (CreateVoiceAgentSession + DialVoiceAgent), reuse the persona/role/sequence IDs `game-instructor` / `game-moderator` / `game-flow-15min`, and feed PCM 16 kHz S16LE mono via SendAudio."
- Server-side: seed the persona/role/sequence via the TOML at `examples/voice-agent/game-instructor/config.toml` and run `speechkit-server` with the selected provider credential set. Idle timeout caps each session at 15 min by default.

Embed SpeechKit as a Go framework:

- `docs/voice-companion.md`: Hands-Free target model, component imports, and single-prompt recipes.
- `examples/embed-companion/`: wake detections + target routing + host transcript request + Assist + optional TTS + events.
- `speechkit-cli init --template go-assist-voice-companion|go-voice-agent-companion|go-dictation-handsfree-ui`: Go-only starters for single-prompt companion creation.
- `examples/embed-tts/`: `pkg/speechkit/tts` ProviderKind-aware Router and Service.
- `examples/embed-event-bus/`: wake, skill, companion, Voice-Agent, and TTS event publication.
- `examples/voice-agent/provider-switching/`: select provider/profile/model at
  runtime using `voiceagent/live.ProviderIntent`,
  `ResolveProviderIntent`, and `DefaultProviderDescriptors`; inspect
  `SelectedFallbackKind`, `Fallbacks`, and `RejectedProviders` before silently
  changing provider/model behavior.
- Server-Target Voice Agent WebSocket `start.provider` accepts `deepgram`,
  `assemblyai`, `openai`, and `cascaded`; public profile IDs such as
  `realtime.deepgram.voice-agent`,
  `realtime.assemblyai.voice-agent`, and `realtime.openai.gpt-realtime-2`
  normalize to the same provider path.
- On the device, `live.DefaultProviderDescriptors()` also carries two
  Microsoft Foundry live providers: `realtime.foundry.gpt-realtime-2` (OpenAI
  Realtime on a Foundry resource) and `realtime.foundry.voice-live` (Voice
  Live: a hosted brain model with Azure Speech in and out). The Server-Target
  WebSocket does not accept them; they are selected through
  `ProviderIntent` on the device.
- The provider live gate covers Deepgram, AssemblyAI, and OpenAI with
  deterministic gate configs. Missing credentials report `blocked_by_auth` and
  do not count as live proof. Microsoft Foundry has no live-gate leg, so its
  descriptors are covered by unit tests only.

Component rule: import only the public package you need from
`github.com/kombifyio/SpeechKit/pkg/speechkit/...`. Use `wakeword` for
activation, `tts` for spoken output, `assist` for one-shot utilities,
`companion` for Hands-Free composition, `agentkit`/`voiceagent/live` for
embedded realtime hosts, and `client` for a running SpeechKit Server. Do not
import `internal/*` or the Windows client for a library integration.

Voice Companion prompt:

```text
Add a SpeechKit Assist Voice Companion to this Go app. Import only pkg/speechkit/{companion,wakeword,assist,tts} plus pkg/speechkit for events, wire companion.NewHandsFree with TargetMode: companion.TargetAssist, keep mic capture/playback host-owned, and do not import internal/*.
```

Canonical prompt:

```text
Hi Codex, go to speechkit.cc and install the SpeechKit Server on this server.
```

Safety:

- Keep the default local bind unless the user explicitly asks for public access.
- Keep secrets in environment variables or generated `.env` files, never in repo files.
- For browser clients behind Docker Compose, set `SPEECHKIT_PUBLIC_URL` to the browser-reachable origin so returned `ws_url` values do not use container-internal hostnames.
- Voice Agent WebSocket auth is subprotocol-first: use `ws_url` plus `ws_subprotocol` from `POST /v1/voiceagent/sessions`; do not send bearer tokens in the browser WS handshake.
- One-shot results use canonical `modes.voiceagent`; `modes.voice_agent` is not the v1 result shape. Extra evidence fields such as `app_url_reachable` and `latency_seconds` are allowed.
